nature_of_interdependence: Seasonal tending of transhumant sheep and goat flocks during summer high-pasture migration
exchange_medium: Free meals, clothing, wool for family, 2-4 sheep per 100 herded, and Rs. 2/month cash wages
direction_of_flow: Bilateral (Labour for subsistence goods + livestock dividend + cash)
historical_significance: Demonstrates internal labour stratification and contractual wage relations within the transhumant pastoral economy

nature_of_interdependence: Wool processing; weaving coarse tweed (pattu) and blankets (gardu); tailoring traditional chola and dora attire
exchange_medium: Shares of sheared raw wool; cooked food during work; seasonal grain perquisites
direction_of_flow: Bilateral (Raw pastoral wool for manufactured garments and service)
historical_significance: Foundational economic interdependence linking upper-caste sheep owners to lower-caste textile specialists

nature_of_interdependence: Shiva Nawala domestic thanksgiving ceremony; animal sacrifice and nocturnal hymn assembly
exchange_medium: Customary neck portion of sacrificed sheep (ghardi) plus unhusked grain and flour
direction_of_flow: Bilateral (Ritual performance for sacred sacrificial meat shares and grain)
historical_significance: Proof of ritual and dietary reciprocity crossing caste boundaries during high-altitude Shaivite festivals

nature_of_interdependence: Overnight penning of migratory sheep/goats on fallow terraced fields (tarkals) during spring transit for soil fertilization
exchange_medium: Grain shares paid by landowners to contractor who passed 50% to shepherd; replaced post-1947 by direct Forest Dept permits
direction_of_flow: Bilateral (Animal manure fertilization in exchange for staple cereal grain)
historical_significance: Crucial agro-pastoral ecological nutrient transfer cycle mediated by state regulation

nature_of_interdependence: Plowing of terraced fields and harvest labour under traditional tenancy rules to maintain high-caste ploughing taboos
exchange_medium: Tied crop share tenancy and customary maintenance grain; contested via Arya Samaj mobilisation for status uplift
direction_of_flow: Bilateral (Attached agricultural labour in exchange for crop share and land access)
historical_significance: Structural agrarian dependence illustrating caste-based division of labour and early 20th-century socio-religious reform

nature_of_interdependence: Supply of fresh milk and butter during monsoon months when local cattle produce almost zero milk (4-8 chhataks/day)
exchange_medium: Cash purchase or grain barter on high alpine ridges (dhars) during rainy season encampments
direction_of_flow: Bilateral (Grain/cash for essential high-fat dairy nutrition)
historical_significance: Direct empirical evidence of seasonal cross-caste and trans-religious trade between settled Hindus and mobile pastoral Muslims

nature_of_interdependence: Performance of sacred pipes and drums at morning/evening worship and seasonal fairs (Navratri/Jatar)
exchange_medium: Customary annual grain collections from village households and stipends from temple endowment
direction_of_flow: Bilateral (Ceremonial musical service for hereditary grain entitlements)
historical_significance: Institutionalised temple service caste functioning within sacred village economy

nature_of_interdependence: Manufacture and repair of iron agricultural tools (ploughshares, sickles, axes) and pastoral implements
exchange_medium: Non-monetary khalian: fixed sheaves of unhusked grain delivered directly from the threshing floor (khala) at each harvest
direction_of_flow: Bilateral (Crucial craft maintenance for seasonal staple food grain)
historical_significance: Definitive evidence of customary non-monetary jajmani barter operating in rural Chamba alongside monetised transactions

nature_of_interdependence: Commercial marketing of high-fat buffalo milk and clarified butter (ghee) derived from village herd of 217 buffaloes
exchange_medium: Cash sales in urban retail markets and advance credit against future ghee deliveries
direction_of_flow: Bilateral (Commodified pastoral surplus for regional currency and manufactured goods)
historical_significance: Micro-pastoral integration into regional market economy transforming subsistence milk into commercial commodity

nature_of_interdependence: Co-existence in fragmented settlement; provision of buffalo dung manure; exchange of draft bullocks; joint upkeep of water points
exchange_medium: Mutual non-monetary reciprocal assistance and neighborly social accommodations during festivals
direction_of_flow: Multilateral (Shared ecological infrastructure and complementary production niches)
historical_significance: Peaceful inter-religious coexistence anchored in complementary economic specialisations rather than competition

nature_of_interdependence: Trans-Himalayan transhumance linking summer alpine grazing in Brahmaur with winter pasturage and wheat cropping in Kangra
exchange_medium: Biannual grazing dues (Rs. 15 per 100 sheep in summer); land revenue paid to both administrations
direction_of_flow: Multilateral (Pastoral mobility navigating political borders and dual property rights)
historical_significance: Historical baseline of regional mobility demonstrating ecological adaptation across political frontiers

nature_of_interdependence: Fabrication of heavy traditional silver ornaments (chiri, ralu, dhodku jhumku, kanbali) used for female adornment and portable savings
exchange_medium: Cash fee per tola of silver crafted plus retention of silver filings and customary food gifts during weddings
direction_of_flow: Bilateral (Precious metal converting coin savings into dowry and social prestige)
historical_significance: Craft specialization transforming pastoral profits (from wool and livestock sales) into portable material culture
